Germanium is warm, woolly, temperature-flaky and cleans up like a dream. Silicon is loud, spitty, aggressive and reliable. You pick a side, you buy the pedal, and you spend the next decade quietly wishing it did the other thing on Tuesdays. GG-ARTICLE-AFTER-INTRO The Vemuram Myriad Fuzz refuses to pick. It puts a silicon transistor and a vintage germanium transistor in the same signal path, gives you a knob called Feel to move between their characters, and hides a trimmer inside the enclosure that biases the germanium side to taste. It is hand-built in Tokyo, wrapped in solid brass, and it costs more than most people’s first amplifier. It is also, unusually for a signature pedal, the leftover half of a much stranger machine — and the guitarist whose name is on it has been photographed using it on his own board for years, which is more than can be said for a lot of endorsements. This is the full story: where the circuit came from, what every control actually does, who genuinely plays one, how to dial it in, and whether the brass justifies the invoice. How to Get the Tone ↓ The short version The Myriad Fuzz is a hybrid germanium/silicon fuzz, hand-built by Vemuram in Tokyo in a solid brass enclosure, developed with American blues guitarist and producer Josh Smith. It has four external knobs — Level, Fuzz, Feel and Tone — plus an internal Germanium Bias trimmer. It runs on a 9-volt battery or a standard centre-negative 9 V supply, is true bypass, and draws a startlingly small amount of current. Its selling point is range. At low Fuzz settings with the Feel knob backed off it behaves like a thick, saturated overdrive with enormous output on tap. Wound up, it goes into Big Muff territory without the mid-scoop, and it retains a low end that vintage Fuzz Face circuits simply do not have. It cleans up off the guitar volume knob the way good germanium fuzzes do, but it does it without the volume drop and tonal collapse that usually comes with that trick. As of September 2026 it is a $435-and-up pedal in the United States, with Equipboard tracking an average across merchants of $462 and a spread up to roughly $558. It sits in the top price tier of the fuzz category, and it knows it. Who Josh Smith is, and why the pedal exists The résumé Josh Smith was born in Middletown, Connecticut on 7 October 1979 and raised in Fort Lauderdale, Florida. sources.excerpt: Vemuram Myriad Fuzz | AllThePedals Articles Genealogy Browse Search results for " " Gain / Fuzz / Vemuram Myriad Fuzz Myriad Fuzz The Vemuram Myriad Fuzz, a collaboration with Josh Smith, is a versatile fuzz pedal blending silicon and vintage germanium transistors. Offering a wide tonal range from spitty to smooth overdrive fuzz, it features a trimmer for germanium bias control, allowing for dynamic and organic fuzz tones. Its design is inspired by the best vintage fuzzes. What Vemuram say about the Myriad Fuzz A collaboration pedal with Josh Smith. The Myriad Fuzz is a hybrid between a Silicon transistor and a vintage Germanium transistor. The range of the tone is very wide and has enough head room to control the fuzz tone from spitty fuzz to a smooth overdrive fuzz. The trimmer allows you to control the Germanium Bias with the FEEL knob which will affect the tone of the fuzz. Josh Smith's Comment "The Myriad fuzz started life as one half of my larger Myriad pedal. When it started to become clear how great the fuzz sounded we knew it would need to be released on its own. This is the fuzz I've had in my mind for over 10 years. A unique fuzz that employ's both Germanium and Silicon transistors. It is incredibly tweak-able but never complicated. There is no bad sounds in this pedal. No matter where you set the knobs you get great tone. It goes from fire breathing silicon to cool warm germanium easily, it cleans up like the best vintage fuzzes, adn is more dynamic and organic than any fuzz has the right to be. It goes from spitty to smooth effortlessly. It also has a large amount of volume on tap and a tone circuit that allows it to really work live. I've wanted this fuzz all my life and thanks to my friends at Vemuram we all now get to enjoy it!!!" www.vemuram.com Myriad Fuzz compared to ...
